Let
\[
\rho_x:=\frac{1-\omega_x}{\omega_x}
=
\begin{cases}
\frac13,&S_x=R,\\[2mm]
3,&S_x=L.
\end{cases}
\]

The environment chain is stationary and ergodic.

### 1. Direction of transience

For a stationary ergodic one-dimensional RWRE, the direction is determined by
\[
\mathbb E_\theta[\log \rho_0].
\]
Here
\[
\mathbb E_\theta[\log\rho_0]
=\theta\log\frac13+(1-\theta)\log3
=(1-2\theta)\log3.
\]
Therefore
\[
\theta_{\rm dir}=\frac12.
\]

Indeed, the walk goes to \(+\infty\) when this expectation is negative, to \(-\infty\) when it is positive, and is recurrent when it is zero.

### 2. Expected time to hit \(+1\)

For a fixed environment, the standard one-dimensional hitting-time expansion is
\[
E_\omega T_1
=
1+2\sum_{n\ge 0}\prod_{j=0}^n \rho_{-j}.
\]
Hence, by Tonelli,
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_1<\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sum_{n\ge0}
\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\prod_{j=0}^n\rho_{-j}\right]<\infty.
\]

The two-state stationary chain is reversible, so the reversed sequence
\((S_0,S_{-1},S_{-2},\dots)\) has transition matrix \(P_{\alpha,\theta}\).

Let
\[
D=\begin{pmatrix}1/3&0\\0&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The above series converges exactly when
\[
r(P_{\alpha,\theta}D)<1,
\]
where \(r(\cdot)\) denotes spectral radius.

Write \(q=1-\alpha\). Then
\[
P_{\alpha,\theta}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\alpha+q\theta&q(1-\theta)\\
q\theta&\alpha+q(1-\theta)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
A direct calculation gives
\[
\det(I-P_{\alpha,\theta}D)
=
\frac{8q\theta+2\alpha-6}{3}.
\]
Since the matrix is positive and one diagonal entry is below \(1\), the condition \(r(P_{\alpha,\theta}D)<1\) is equivalent to positivity of this determinant. Thus
\[
8(1-\alpha)\theta+2\alpha-6>0,
\]
or
\[
\theta>\frac{3-\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\theta_+=\frac{3-\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)}.
\]

### 3. Expected time to hit \(-1\)

Similarly,
\[
E_\omega T_{-1}
=
1+2\sum_{n\ge0}\prod_{j=0}^n \rho_j^{-1}.
\]
Let
\[
D^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1/3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_\theta T_{-1}<\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r(P_{\alpha,\theta}D^{-1})<1.
\]
Again,
\[
\det(I-P_{\alpha,\theta}D^{-1})
=
\frac{2-6\alpha-8(1-\alpha)\theta}{3}.
\]
Thus finiteness is equivalent to
\[
2-6\alpha-8(1-\alpha)\theta>0,
\]
which gives
\[
\theta<\frac{1-3\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\theta_-=\frac{1-3\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)}.
\]

Since \(0<\alpha<1/3\),
\[
0<\theta_-<\frac12<\theta_+<1.
\]

Hence the requested triple is
\[
\boxed{
\left(
\theta_-,
\theta_{\rm dir},
\theta_+
\right)
=
\left(
\frac{1-3\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)},
\frac12,
\frac{3-\alpha}{4(1-\alpha)}
\right).
}
\]
